nuggets.text: The Redbirds' 76-0 opener over St. Francis was their second-highest score ever, behind 80 points against Eureka in 1937.
The Redbirds scored touchdowns on their first 10 drives against St. Francis, and their passers started 20-for-20.
The Redbirds' win at Western Illinois was their 10th straight FCS road win, the longest active streak in the FCS.
Last season the Redbirds became the first team in FCS history to win four straight road playoff games.
The Redbirds stunned No. 1 North Dakota State 29-28 in Fargo last December, snapping a 14-game losing streak to the Bison.
Brock Spack, a former Purdue linebacker and defensive coordinator, is the winningest coach in Illinois State history.
Last season, brothers Tye and Dexter Niekamp played linebacker for their dad, Redbirds defensive coordinator Travis Niekamp.
Tye Niekamp led the entire FCS with 160 tackles last season and was named MVFC Defensive Player of the Year.
Illinois State's teams were once the Fighting Teachers; a sports editor coined Redbirds to set them apart from the St. Louis Cardinals.
The Redbirds and Huskies first met in 1906, a 6-5 Northern Illinois win, and last played in 2019.
